titleStmt.title: Telegram From the Embassy in Venezuela to the Department of State

div.head: 485. Telegram From the Embassy in Venezuela to the Department of State
div.p: 6123. Subject: Ambassador’s call on President Carlos Andres Perez.

2. Summary: Ambassador met with President-elect Carlos Andres Perez (CAP) on December 28 to follow up on issues discussed at CAP’s meeting with President-elect Bush in Washington on December 13. Issues discussed included:

list.item: CAP’s perception of the Bush-CAP meeting;
Oil prices and possible SPR sales by Venezuela to the U.S.;
CAP’s inauguration and possible participation by Castro and Ortega;
Tenure of current U.S. Ambassador to Venezuela;
Trade and investment, including barter arrangements.

div.p: These issues will be reported by septels. Throughout the meeting CAP was short on specifics but appeared very pleased by his conversation with President-elect Bush. End summary.

3. General perception of CAP-Bush meeting: CAP spoke at length and very warmly about his meeting with President-elect Bush. He used a number of adjectives such as “warm,” “open,” “knowledgeable,” “sensible,” “understanding,” and “strong” to describe President-elect Bush. He was, as we have heard from various sources in the CAP team, obviously pleased with the personal treatment accorded him by Vice President Bush, including the “extra” unexpected gestures by the Vice President such as meeting CAP at the driveway, accompanying him and presenting him to the press corps, and finally taking him personally to his limousine and waiting until the departure of CAP’s motorcade. This Embassy has heard from various sources that the Venezuelans were extremely impressed by the courtesies accorded to CAP by the person they consider to be the most important man in the world after January 20, 1989.

The Ambassador has been told that CAP has stated, “He (Bush) treated me as an equal,” not only in the courtesies extended but in truly listening to CAP’s opinion and eliciting his suggestions and recommendations.

4. Embassy believes that, although differences of opinion are bound to emerge between the U.S. and Venezuelan administrations which are to take office on January 20 and February 2 respectively, the CAP-Bush meeting has created an opportunity for close cooperation, at least in the short term, on extremely important hemispheric issues.

note.p: Source: George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Vice Presidential Records, Office of National Security Affairs, Donald P. Gregg Files, OA/ID 19874–015, Country Files, Venezuela–1988. Secret; Immediate. Printed from a copy that indicates the original was received in the White House Situation Room. An unknown hand wrote “GOOD VIBES!” in the right-hand margin.

A memorandum of conversation of Bush’s December 13 meeting with Pérez is ibid. In telegram 393002 to Caracas, December 6, the Department forwarded Reagan’s letter of congratulations to Pérez on his election as President.
